meaningful_changes.change: Server documentation now explicitly documents MCP stdio servers, tool naming and CORS defaults, including the warning that spawned MCP servers run with llama-server privileges and that tool-enabled deployments should constrain origins.
meaningful_changes.eay_impact: EAY local-first inference can use llama.cpp MCP capability only behind the existing Jarvis tool-execution boundary. MCP child processes must be treated as privileged code execution, with isolated process/container identity, scoped filesystem/egress and explicit CORS/origin policy. Do not expose raw llama-server tool execution directly to end users.

meaningful_changes.change: Ollama updated its MLX runtime after the earlier llama.cpp update.
meaningful_changes.eay_impact: Local serving upgrades must be version-pinned and evaluated as runtime bundles rather than treating Ollama and its underlying inference backends independently. Apple/MLX paths need the same EAY model/eval manifest and regression gates before adoption.

meaningful_changes.change: Red-team grading now preserves cumulative grading token usage instead of losing aggregate usage accounting.
meaningful_changes.eay_impact: This directly improves local-token-minimization and eval cost governance. EAY evaluation records should preserve cumulative token/cost counters across grader passes so regressions cannot look cheaper due to accounting loss. Promptfoo remains evaluation tooling, not a sandbox or authorization authority.

meaningful_changes.change: Phoenix introduced a trace-level expression filter DSL with server-side validation, compiler-derived vocabulary, trace/span annotation filtering, quantifiers/reductions and SQLite/PostgreSQL differential semantics tests.
meaningful_changes.eay_impact: Useful reference for EAY observability/query UX: expressive trace filters should compile through a server-authoritative typed grammar, validate against known vocabulary and retain entity scope. This must not replace EAY tenant/provenance authorization. Phoenix remains REFERENCE due to Elastic-2.0 hosted-service restrictions.

meaningful_changes.change: Dashboard filter scope is now derived on read rather than served from stale cached scope, and dataset metric certification preserves certified_by metadata while certification details are edited.
meaningful_changes.eay_impact: Both changes matter to governed EAY Insight/KPI embedding. Scope metadata must be recalculated from authoritative state rather than trusted from stale dashboard cache, and promoted KPI certification provenance must survive UI edits. Superset remains a projection/analytics layer; EAY KPI truth and tenant/store/entity scope stay server-authoritative in Platform/Jarvis contracts.
